answer: An operator's identities share one thread. The kth must sail a voyage as long as that operator's prior voyages combined, paying out that much thread, and each port on the voyage signs a whisper at the thread's new end. Ports sign only a voyage begun at the last whisper, so a fresh wallet inherits the spooled length. The added identity costs as much as all earlier ones together and cannot be funded in parallel. One identity pays one link; the tenth 256 links; the thousandth 2^998 links.
